after: ## Central concepts and the learner portfolio
alt: Three areas of exploration, readers, writers and texts; time and space; and intertextuality: connecting texts, each 50 hours at SL and 80 at HL and each drawing on literary and non-literary texts. Seven central concepts run across all three, and the learner portfolio underpins them.
caption: Every area mixes literary works with non-literary texts.

alt: SL students study at least 4 literary works: at least 1 originally written in the language studied, at least 1 in translation and 2 freely chosen. HL students study at least 6: 2, 2 and 2. Non-literary texts of equivalent teaching time are added in each area.
caption: SL: at least 4 works; HL: at least 6, plus equal time on non-literary texts.

alt: Paper 1, guided textual analysis, uses unseen non-literary passages. Paper 2, the comparative essay, is set on literary works only. The individual oral connects one literary work and one non-literary body of work to a global issue. The HL essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words can be on a literary work or a non-literary body of work.
caption: Paper 1 is non-literary, Paper 2 is literary: revise them as separate tracks.
